column2: What does the “🌾 Their terroir” block show?
column3: The PDO and PGI products of their municipality (when their trade relates to them: winegrower, cheesemaker…), the animal breeds of their region, the headdress and costume of their region (also useful for dating a family photo), the schools of the past in the municipality, and the meaning of their first name and surname (Wiktionary). The data comes with the app: only a first name or surname goes on the Internet, never for a confidential record or a living person. Each part is turned on or off in Settings → “🌾 Their terroir”.

column2: What does the “🪨 Land and words of their country” block show?
column3: The soil of their village (the rock, the altitude), the village’s name in the regional language and the name of its inhabitants, vanished villages, old fruit varieties of their region, sundials, a few words of the French of their area, old measures, legends and great fears of their lifetime, the great criminal cases of the region (never linked to your family), festivals, their name given to an asteroid or a rose, and their famous namesakes (online, never merged). Each part is set in Settings → “🪨 Land and words of the village”.

column2: What does the “🎡 The world of their village” block show?
column3: Shows premiered in the year of their marriage (otherwise at age 20), the sports clubs of their town, the Tour de France at their home, the World’s Fair of their time, the coincidences of their life (born, married or died on the day of a great event), the lord of their village before 1789, vanished churches and the fairs of their region. You also find it on a village’s record and in the monograph; the lists are in Lists. Choose the parts in Settings → “🎡 The village world”.

column2: What does the “🌟 Around their life” block (Wikidata) show?
column3: Famous people born in the same place (within 50 years) or on the same day, their famous namesakes (same name, not necessarily family), the great events nearby during their life and the hit song in the year of their birth, each line with “↗ Wikidata”. The Wikidata data (CC0) comes with the app: everything works without the Internet, only the ↗ links open the web. When you type a place, a small line also recognises a former name (“Lemberg” → Lviv). Settings → “🌟 Wikidata”: the switch, what is shown, the distance.

column2: What is the “🔎 What concerns them” block for?
column3: It gathers what the app’s data can say about a person: the best suggestions first (with “↗ source”), the rest under “▸ see the N”. “✓ Keep” puts a suggestion on their record in one click (as a note with its source, as a source alone or as a “context” event); “＋ Also add to…” copies it to their spouse, children, parents…; “✗ Not useful” hides it. “⤢ See all” opens the full report (The person, Their places, Their time, To look for) and offers to install what is missing. On a village’s record: “What concerns this place”.

column2: How do I hide the relationship shown at the top of the record?
column3: The record’s ⋯ menu → “🧭 Hide the relationship” (then “Show the relationship” to bring it back). The choice applies to all records and is remembered; “↶ Undo” is offered right away.

column2: What does the “🔔 Objects and traces” block show?
column3: The bells of their municipality and their inscriptions (godfather, godmother, priest… when a name from your database can be read there), the village’s objects in museums, plants picked in their municipality in their lifetime (herbaria), plaques and steles, tales and songs collected near their home, the pilgrimages of their region, the hospices near the place of their death and, for a woman, the convents nearby at age 20. Only the INSEE code, the position or the name of the municipality goes on the Internet, nothing for a living or confidential record. Settings → “🔔 Objects and traces”.

column2: What does “⚖️ The rules of their life” show, and where are the aids for reading records?
column3: On the record: the custom of their land before 1789 (and what it said about dividing the inheritance), the salt tax in their lifetime, their marriage and the closed times (Advent, Lent), the sayings of their birthday, the wind and the traditional “pays” of their municipality. In 📖 Reading help: Latin abbreviations (Cappelli), handwriting models of the period, the meaning of old words (online) and “📅 Feast → date” (“le jour de la Saint-Martin 1702” → the exact date). Settings → “⚖️ Rules and records”.

column2: How can I see my ancestor’s village as they saw it?
column3: The “🖼️ Their village as they saw it” block: museum paintings depicting their municipality (those painted in their lifetime), old photos (1850–1950) with the one closest to age 20, the village seen from the air around 1950 next to today, the woods of 1850 (did they live on the edge of a vanished wood?) and, on request, what could be seen from their home, the hidden traces of the laser relief and the houses of their time still standing. Each place is requested online once, then kept; nothing for a confidential record or a living person. Settings → “🖼️ See their village”.

column2: What does “⛰️ Their land and its people” show?
column3: The dangers of their land (avalanches, landslides, quarries for a quarryman, volcanoes that ruined the harvests, wrecks offshore for a sailor) and the people and places around them: the map of their name (INSEE deaths already imported), the post relays on their route, the walking time to their spouse (relief included), the parcel of a locality on today’s cadastre, their village in Algeria, Quebec heritage, the Historical Dictionary of Switzerland and the 1950 US census. Settings → “⛰️ Their land and its people”.

column2: How do I make the record of a castle or a church?
column3: On a village’s record or in the monograph: “🏰⛪ The buildings of the municipality” → “＋ Make a record” (also from the small card of a Wikidata castle, or from a record: “🔗 Link to a record card?” when the address mentions a castle or a church). The record gathers its history, its lords or priests, your family’s records that took place there, its registers, its protected objects and its sources; what comes from Wikidata or Mérimée is only copied when you click. All your records: Settings → “🏰⛪ Building records”.

column2: How do I create a territory from municipalities?
column3: Map → “🧩 My territories” box → “manage” (or, in the vector drawing, Plan menu → “🧩 Territory from towns…”). Choose the municipalities by searching a name or a code, by clicking on the map, “all the municipalities of” a département, an arrondissement or a canton, or from the places in your database: their shared borders disappear. Give it a name, a colour, hatching, a label; it is kept and can be changed later. It can be placed on the Map, in the diagram maps and in the drawing, and serves as an “in the territory” filter in the Lists.

column2: How do I put open data on a map?
column3: On a diagram map (Charts → Maps): “＋ Data”; in the vector drawing: Plan menu → “＋ Open data on the plan (earthquakes, castles, places…)…”. Choose a source (a dataset from the Lists, your territories, the country borders of a given year, the places in your database, earthquakes, weather stations…), filters (text, years, category, around a place, in a territory) and a style. The layer has its legend line and the credit of its source, is kept with the diagram and goes with the export.

column2: How do I arrange or hide the parts of the municipality monograph?
column3: Charts → Municipality monograph → “⚙︎ Customize”: drag ⠿ (or ↑ ↓) for the order, untick to hide, “↶ Reset” to go back to the start; for all municipalities or “only for this municipality”. Printing and export follow the chosen order; a part that is empty for this municipality is skipped automatically.

column2: How do I search the app’s datasets (Lists → Data)?
column3: Lists → “🧰 Data”: each dataset (castles, schools, fairs, wrecks…) has its list, with the same way of searching everywhere: combined criteria, “📅 Period” (in the year, entirely between, overlapping), “📍 Around” a municipality within N km, free search, sorting, Table or 🗺 Map, ⤓ Export (CSV), 🖨 Print and saved searches (★). A pack not yet installed offers “⤓ Install”. “🔎 Search all the data” lists, for a person, a place or a year, every dataset that can say something about it.
